title: Scheduling & Automation
brief: Implement cron jobs, batch operations, and automated maintenance using CronCreate/CronDelete/CronList and /batch skill. Currently NO scheduled tasks exist. Add: hourly build health, 6h test regression, 12h dispatcher sync, 12h schema drift, daily catalog freshness, daily memory pruning, weekly dead code, weekly vulnerability scan, weekly doc coverage, weekly hook efficiency, monthly automation ROI.

phases.title: Cron Jobs & Batch Automation
phases.description: Create all scheduled cron jobs for build health, test regression, dispatcher sync, schema drift, catalog freshness, memory cleanup, dead code, vulnerabilities, doc coverage, hook efficiency, and ROI reporting. Wire batch skill for parallel operations.

units.title: Build health cron
units.rationale: Hourly build health checks catch regressions early, preventing broken builds from accumulating. CronCreate every 1h runs esbuild + reports errors to a status file.
exit_conditions: Cron created and firing on 1h schedule
Build errors written to state/CCM-MS5/build-health.json
CronList shows the cron entry

steps.instruction: Create state/CCM-MS5/ directory for cron output artifacts.
Write build-health-cron.sh script that runs prism-build.sh, captures exit code and stderr, writes JSON report to state/CCM-MS5/build-health.json with timestamp and status.
Use CronCreate to schedule build-health-cron.sh every 1 hour.
Verify with CronList that the cron is registered and firing.

units.description: Build health cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Test regression cron
units.rationale: Every 6h full test suite run catches regressions before they compound. Tracks pass rate over time to detect degradation trends.
exit_conditions: Cron tracks test pass rate in state/CCM-MS5/test-regression.json
History of pass/fail counts maintained across runs
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write test-regression-cron.sh that runs vitest with JSON reporter, parses pass/fail/skip counts, appends to test-regression.json with timestamp.
Use CronCreate to schedule every 6 hours.
Verify cron output after first manual trigger.

units.description: Test regression cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Dispatcher sync cron
units.rationale: Engine-to-dispatcher wiring drift is a recurring issue. Every 12h verification catches new engines that lack dispatcher actions or orphaned actions pointing to missing engines.
exit_conditions: Mismatches auto-detected and written to state/CCM-MS5/dispatcher-sync.json
Report includes unwired engines and orphaned actions
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write dispatcher-sync-cron.sh that scans src/engines/ exports vs dispatcher z.enum entries, reports mismatches.
Use CronCreate to schedule every 12 hours.
Validate by intentionally checking known wired vs unwired engines.

units.description: Dispatcher sync cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Memory cleanup cron
units.rationale: Memory files accumulate stale entries that waste context tokens. Weekly pruning archives entries referencing deleted files or completed milestones older than 30 days.
exit_conditions: Stale entries archived to state/CCM-MS5/memory-archive/
MEMORY.md index updated after pruning
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write memory-cleanup-cron.sh that scans memory/*.md files for references to non-existent paths, completed milestones >30d old.
Archive pruned entries to state/CCM-MS5/memory-archive/ with timestamps.
Use CronCreate to schedule weekly.
Verify archive contains expected pruned entries after manual trigger.

units.description: Memory cleanup cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Catalog freshness cron
units.rationale: Tool/material/machine catalogs should be checked daily for staleness — files not updated in 90+ days may have outdated data or missing new entries from manufacturer updates.
exit_conditions: Stale catalogs flagged in state/CCM-MS5/catalog-freshness.json
Report includes file path, last modified, and days stale
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write catalog-freshness-cron.sh that checks mtime of all *-catalog*.ts files in src/data/, flags any >90 days old.
Output JSON report with file, lastModified, daysStalee, and staleness tier (warning/critical).
Use CronCreate to schedule daily.

units.description: Catalog freshness cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Batch skill updater
units.rationale: With 132+ skills, updating frontmatter or patterns across all of them manually is error-prone. Batch integration enables parallel worktree updates.
features: Batch skill frontmatter updates across 132+ skills
exit_conditions: Batch updates work across all 132+ skills in parallel worktrees
Frontmatter changes applied consistently
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write batch-skill-update.sh that enumerates all skill files, applies a given sed/jq transformation to each.
Integrate with /batch skill for parallel worktree execution.
Test with a no-op transformation to verify all skills processed.

units.description: Batch skill updater — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Batch test runner
units.rationale: Running 17K+ tests sequentially is slow. Batch integration splits test suites by domain and runs in parallel worktrees for faster feedback.
entry_conditions: Batch skill integration from P0-U06 working
exit_conditions: Parallel test execution works across at least 4 domain splits
Results aggregated into unified report
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Define domain splits: engines/, algorithms/, dispatchers/, integration/.
Write batch-test-runner.sh that launches vitest per domain in parallel worktrees.
Aggregate results into state/CCM-MS5/batch-test-results.json.
Verify all domains complete and results merge correctly.

units.description: Batch test runner — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Cron management skill
units.rationale: A /cron-manage skill provides a unified interface to list, create, and delete crons without remembering tool names or parameter formats.
entry_conditions: At least one cron exists from P0-U01
exit_conditions: Skill lists all active crons
Skill creates new crons with validated schedule
Skill deletes crons by ID

steps.instruction: Create /cron-manage skill file with list/create/delete subcommands.
Wire CronList for listing, CronCreate for creation with schedule validation, CronDelete for removal.
Test all three operations end-to-end.

units.title: Schema drift cron
units.rationale: Dispatcher z.enum schemas drift when new engines are added but their actions are not registered. Every 12h scan catches this before it causes runtime failures.
entry_conditions: Dispatcher sync cron from P0-U03 exists as reference
exit_conditions: Drift auto-detected: z.enum entries vs engine exports compared
Missing actions listed in state/CCM-MS5/schema-drift.json
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write schema-drift-cron.sh that extracts z.enum values from all dispatcher files and compares against exported engine action methods.
Report missing and orphaned entries.
Use CronCreate to schedule every 12 hours.

units.description: Schema drift cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Dead code detection cron
units.rationale: With 1078 engine files, dead code accumulates. Weekly scan identifies unexported or unreferenced engines that could be pruned to reduce bundle size.
exit_conditions: Unexported/unreferenced engine candidates listed in state/CCM-MS5/dead-code.json
Report includes file path and reason (unexported/unreferenced)
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write dead-code-cron.sh that checks each engine file against index.ts exports and import references across the codebase.
Flag engines not exported from index.ts or not imported anywhere.
Use CronCreate to schedule weekly.

units.description: Dead code detection cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.rationale: npm audit should run weekly to catch new CVEs. Critical vulnerabilities auto-create a task for immediate attention.
features: Weekly vulnerability scanning with auto-task creation
exit_conditions: Vulnerabilities detected and reported in state/CCM-MS5/vuln-scan.json
Critical vulns auto-create a task via TaskCreate
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write vuln-scan-cron.sh that runs npm audit --json, parses severity counts.
If critical count > 0, use TaskCreate to create a fix task.
Use CronCreate to schedule weekly.

units.description: Dependency vulnerability cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Documentation coverage cron
units.rationale: JSDoc coverage is at 97/100 (8,853 blocks). Weekly measurement ensures new code maintains coverage and flags gaps before they accumulate.
exit_conditions: Coverage tracked in state/CCM-MS5/doc-coverage.json
New gaps flagged with file path and function name
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

Compare against previous run to detect coverage drops.
Use CronCreate to schedule weekly.

units.title: Hook efficiency cron
units.rationale: 213 hookify rules need periodic efficiency review — fire rates, false positive rates, and latency impact. Weekly analysis identifies underperforming or redundant rules.
exit_conditions: Efficiency metrics produced in state/CCM-MS5/hook-efficiency.json
Metrics include fire count, false positive rate, avg latency per hook
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write hook-efficiency-cron.sh that parses hook execution logs, calculates fire rate, false positive rate, and latency per hook.
Flag hooks with >50% false positive rate or >500ms avg latency.
Use CronCreate to schedule weekly.

units.description: Hook efficiency cron — follow 4-LOOP (BUILD → SCRUTINIZE → GAP FILL → TIE UP), consult KNOWLEDGE_SOURCES before coding, forge-triple ownership in milestone header.

units.title: Automation ROI report cron
units.rationale: Monthly ROI report quantifies token savings from all automation (hooks, crons, batch ops) vs manual baseline, justifying continued investment in automation infrastructure.
entry_conditions: Hook efficiency data available from P0-U13
exit_conditions: ROI report generated in state/CCM-MS5/automation-roi.json
Report includes token savings, time savings, and cost reduction estimates
Tests pass: npx vitest run (min 10 cases for engine units)

steps.instruction: Write automation-roi-cron.sh that aggregates data from all cron outputs, hook efficiency metrics, and session token ledger.
Calculate token savings vs estimated manual baseline (e.g., manual build check = 500 tokens, automated = 0).
Produce summary ROI report with total savings, per-automation breakdown, and trend.
Use CronCreate to schedule monthly.
